title: AI Lead Follow-Up Automation
shortDescription: We design and implement custom follow-up workflows that reply quickly, qualify interest, and route ready opportunities to your team.
heroHeading: Respond to New Leads Before They Go Cold

seo.seoDescription: We design and implement custom AI lead follow-up automation for US businesses — faster response, qualification, and routing to your team.

children.text: The Business Problem
Most lost leads are not a product problem — they are a timing and follow-up problem. When enquiries sit unanswered, competitors win the conversation.
New form fills, chat messages, and inbound emails wait too long for a reply
Sales teams spend hours on repetitive first-touch and qualification work
Hot leads and low-intent enquiries look the same until someone reviews them manually
Handoffs between marketing, sales, and ops get messy when tools do not talk to each other
What We Build
We build custom AI-assisted follow-up systems around your offers, qualification rules, and CRM — not a one-size product you configure yourself.
Instant, on-brand first responses when a new lead comes in
Qualification flows that ask the right questions and score interest
Smart routing so qualified opportunities reach the right person or inbox
Reminder and nurture sequences for leads that are not ready yet
Clear human handoffs when a conversation needs a person
What You Walk Away With
Concrete artifacts and working systems — not a slide deck that leaves your team guessing.
Documented lead sources, qualification rules, and escalation map
Working follow-up workflows connected to your CRM and messaging channels
Approved reply scripts / prompt guardrails your team can edit
Owner routing, tags, and field updates tested with real sample leads
Handoff playbook: when automation stops and a person takes over
Brief runbook so your team knows how to monitor and adjust
How The Solution Works
We start from the outcome you need — faster response and cleaner pipeline — then design the workflow your team will actually run.
Capture every enquiry
We connect the channels you already use — website forms, landing pages, chat, or inbound email — into one follow-up path.
Respond and qualify
We design automated replies and qualification questions that match your tone and only escalate what meets your criteria.
Route to the right owner
Qualified leads land in your CRM, Slack, email, or assignment rules so your team picks up ready conversations — not noise.
Keep people in control
We define when automation stops and a human takes over, so customers never feel stuck talking to a dead-end bot.
Example Use Cases
Website lead response
A prospect submits a contact form at 9pm. They get a helpful reply within minutes, answer a few qualifying questions, and a sales owner is notified if they meet your criteria.
Service business intake
Home services, clinics, or agencies automatically gather location, urgency, and budget signals before a coordinator schedules the next step.
B2B demo request triage
Demo requests are sorted by company size, use case, and timeline so AEs spend time on opportunities that fit — not every form fill equally.
Missed-call and chat follow-up
When someone leaves a message or abandons chat, a follow-up sequence re-engages them and books them into the right calendar or queue.
Integrations
We connect the tools you already run. The goal is fewer copy-paste steps — not forcing a rip-and-replace stack.
CRMs such as HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive, or custom databases
Forms and landing pages (Webflow, WordPress, Typeform, custom sites)
Email and messaging (Gmail, Outlook, Slack, SMS providers)
Calendars for booking qualified conversations
Spreadsheets and internal ops tools where teams still work today
Who It Is For
Best fit for US businesses where speed-to-lead and consistent qualification directly affect revenue.
Sales and marketing teams drowning in first-touch follow-up
Service businesses that receive form and chat enquiries daily
B2B companies that need cleaner demo and discovery routing
Operators who want automation without buying a rigid packaged product
Where Automation Stops
We design honest boundaries so leads and customers are not trapped in a bot loop.
Pricing negotiations, custom proposals, and relationship closes stay with humans
We do not promise specific conversion-rate lifts — outcomes depend on your offer, traffic, and follow-through
Channels we cannot access (restricted inboxes, unsupported CRMs) stay out of scope until connected
Complex legal, medical, or regulated advice is excluded from automated replies by design
If qualification rules are unclear, we pause automation expansion until you approve them

features.title: Design

features.title: Build & integrate

faqs.question: Is this a product we buy seats for?
faqs.answer: No. We design and implement a custom follow-up system for your business. You keep ownership of the workflows and the accounts we connect — we are not selling a packaged AI product with monthly seats.

faqs.question: How long does a typical engagement take?
faqs.answer: Most focused lead follow-up builds land in a few weeks once we have access to your tools and clear qualification rules. Timeline depends on how many channels and CRM edge cases we need to cover.

faqs.question: What do you need from us to get started?
faqs.answer: Access to the systems where leads arrive today, examples of good replies, your qualification criteria, and a decision-maker who can approve routing rules. We do not need a perfect process — mapping the messy reality is part of discovery.

faqs.question: Who owns the systems and data?
faqs.answer: You do. We build on your CRM, inboxes, and preferred infrastructure wherever practical. Credentials stay under your control, and we document what was built so your team is not locked into undocumented magic.

faqs.question: Will this replace our salespeople?
faqs.answer: No. The goal is to handle repetitive first response and qualification so your people spend time on conversations that matter. We design explicit handoffs to humans for pricing, exceptions, and relationship work.

faqs.question: What if our process is messy today?
faqs.answer: That is normal. We start by documenting how work actually happens, then automate the highest-friction steps first — usually speed-to-lead and routing — before expanding.

title: AI Voice Agents
shortDescription: We design and implement custom voice agents that answer routine questions, qualify callers, and help schedule — then hand off to your team when a person should take over.
heroHeading: Handle Common Inbound Calls Without Missing the Important Ones

seo.seoDescription: We design and implement custom inbound AI voice agents that handle common calls, qualify callers, and help schedule — with clear human handoffs.

children.text: The Business Problem
Missed and repetitive inbound calls drain time and lose revenue. Front desks and sales lines spend hours answering the same questions while urgent callers wait.
After-hours and peak-hour calls go to voicemail
Staff repeat the same FAQs, availability checks, and intake questions
Callers who need a human get stuck in rigid phone trees
Appointment and lead details never make it cleanly into your CRM or calendar
What We Build
We build inbound voice experiences tailored to your scripts, hours, and escalation rules — not a generic call-bot you rent seats for.
Natural inbound call handling for common questions and intake
Caller qualification based on your criteria
Scheduling support against your real calendar rules
Warm or cold handoff to a person when needed
Call summaries and structured data written back to your systems
What You Walk Away With
A production-ready inbound voice path scoped to the call types you approved — with documentation your team can operate.
Call intent map: automate vs escalate vs message-only
Conversation scripts, disclosures, and guardrails you signed off on
Telephony / number routing connected to calendars and CRM where in scope
Booking or callback flows tested against your real availability rules
Transfer and fallback paths to live staff or voicemail
Post-call summary and logging format your team can review
How The Solution Works
We design the conversation around what callers need and what your team must approve — then connect telephony, calendars, and CRM.
Define call intents
We document the call types you want automation to handle versus escalate — FAQs, intake, booking, billing questions, and exceptions.
Design the conversation
We write prompts, guardrails, and confirmation steps so the agent stays on-brand and never invents policies you did not approve.
Connect phone and systems
We integrate your number or call path with calendars, CRM, and notification channels your team already uses.
Test and hand off
We run realistic call scenarios, tune interruptions and silence handling, and confirm that humans can take over cleanly.
Example Use Cases
After-hours answering
Callers outside business hours get answers to common questions and can request a callback or book the next available slot.
Appointment scheduling
The agent checks availability, confirms details, and books — then notifies staff when something needs review.
Lead qualification by phone
Inbound sales calls are screened for service area, budget, or urgency before a closer is interrupted.
Front-desk overflow
During peak volume, routine callers are handled automatically while priority or complex cases ring through to staff.
Integrations
Voice only helps if it connects to how your business already runs scheduling and follow-up.
Phone numbers and call routing (existing providers where possible)
Google Calendar, Outlook, or industry scheduling tools
CRM and helpdesk systems for caller records
SMS and email for confirmations and callbacks
Internal alerts in Slack or team inboxes
Who It Is For
A strong fit when inbound call volume includes many repeatable conversations — and missing calls has a clear cost.
Clinics, home services, and local businesses with heavy phone intake
Sales teams that need after-hours coverage without a full night desk
Operations leaders who want consistent intake quality
Teams that need human escalation for complex or sensitive calls
Where The Voice Agent Hand Offs
Voice automation works for repeatable intake — not for every sensitive or high-stakes conversation.
Medical diagnosis, legal advice, and payment-card capture can be excluded or handed to humans by design
We do not claim the agent will sound indistinguishable from a trained receptionist in every edge case
Carrier, SIP, or legacy PBX constraints may limit how cleanly we can integrate your existing number
Background noise, heavy accents, and overlapping speakers can reduce accuracy — we plan fallbacks
Live close-the-sale or clinical counseling calls stay with people unless you explicitly expand scope after a successful pilot

processDescription: Voice projects succeed when scripts, edge cases, and handoffs are designed before go-live — not bolted on later.

features.title: Discover
features.description: We listen to how calls work today, which questions repeat, and where callers get frustrated.

features.title: Design
features.description: We define intents, escalation rules, booking logic, and what the agent must never say or do.

features.title: Build & integrate
features.description: We implement the agent, connect phone and backend systems, and iterate on real test calls with your team.

features.title: Launch & monitor
features.description: We roll out carefully, review transcripts and outcomes, and refine prompts and routing.

faqs.question: Is this a seat-based voice product?
faqs.answer: No. We design and implement a custom inbound voice agent for your call types and systems. You are not buying a generic packaged product with per-seat pricing from TechVerge.

faqs.question: Will callers know they are speaking with automation?
faqs.answer: We follow the disclosure approach you approve. Many clients prefer clear, professional transparency plus a fast path to a human — we design that into the flow.

faqs.question: What happens when the agent cannot help?
faqs.answer: We define escalation rules up front: transfer to a person, take a message, book a callback, or send a summary to your team. The agent should not trap callers in a loop.

faqs.question: How do you handle sensitive information?
faqs.answer: We scope what the agent is allowed to collect, store, and say. Payment details, medical advice, and other sensitive topics can be excluded or handed to humans by design.

faqs.question: What do you need from our side?
faqs.answer: Sample call recordings or scripts if available, hours of operation, booking rules, FAQs, and access to calendar/CRM systems. A stakeholder who can approve tone and escalation is essential.

faqs.question: How long until we can take live calls?
faqs.answer: A focused inbound use case often reaches a pilot in a few weeks after access and scripts are ready. Broader multi-intent rollouts take longer because testing edge cases matters.

title: Business Process Automation
shortDescription: We design and implement automations across forms, CRM, email, calendars, and internal systems so your team spends less time on repetitive admin.
heroHeading: Connect Your Tools So Work Moves Without Copy-Paste

seo.seoDescription: We design and implement custom business automation that connects forms, CRM, email, calendars, and internal systems — reducing repetitive admin.

children.text: The Business Problem
Growing teams lose hours every week to manual updates between tools. The work is invisible until hiring cannot keep up with the admin load.
Staff re-enter the same data into CRM, spreadsheets, and email
Approvals and status updates live in inboxes instead of a clear workflow
Calendars, forms, and project tools do not stay in sync
Handoffs between sales, delivery, and finance depend on someone remembering to update a field
What We Build
We implement practical automations that move information and tasks between the systems you already use — designed around your process, not a generic template.
Form-to-CRM and form-to-ops pipelines that create clean records
Email and notification flows tied to real status changes
Calendar and scheduling sync for bookings and reminders
Internal task creation when deals, tickets, or requests change stage
Lightweight dashboards or digests so owners see what needs attention
What You Walk Away With
Stable automations for the workflow we scoped — plus the maps and alerts your ops owner needs.
Process map of the target workflow before and after automation
Field mapping and trigger definitions between your connected tools
Working integrations for the agreed happy path and critical exceptions
Error alerts / retry behavior documented for the ops owner
Training notes so the people living with the workflow can spot failures
Prioritized backlog of the next processes worth automating
How The Solution Works
We prioritize the bottlenecks that cost the most time, then connect systems with clear ownership and failure handling.
Map the busywork
We document repetitive steps, tools involved, and where errors or delays usually appear.
Design the happy path
We define triggers, data mapping, approvals, and what happens when something fails or needs a human.
Connect systems
We integrate the apps your team already trusts and add custom logic where off-the-shelf connectors fall short.
Stabilize and expand
We monitor early runs, fix edge cases, then extend automation to the next high-friction process.
Example Use Cases
New client onboarding
When a deal closes, kick off welcome emails, create project folders or tasks, and notify the delivery owner — without a checklist someone forgets.
Lead and ticket hygiene
Normalize form data, enrich records, assign owners, and close the loop when a ticket sits too long.
Scheduling and reminders
Keep calendars, confirmation emails, and CRM activities aligned when appointments are booked or rescheduled.
Ops status digests
Send daily or weekly summaries of open items, stalled deals, or missing fields so managers coach from a single view.
Integrations
We meet you in your current stack. The win is fewer manual bridges — not forcing a new suite overnight.
CRMs and helpdesks
Forms, website backends, and Typeform-style tools
Gmail, Outlook, and team chat
Google Workspace / Microsoft 365 calendars and Drive
Accounting, project, and industry tools via API where available
Who It Is For
Ideal for operators and founders who feel the admin tax of growth before they feel ready for a full software rebuild.
Teams juggling CRM, email, and spreadsheets that never stay aligned
Agencies and service businesses with repetitive onboarding steps
Ops leaders who want reliable handoffs between departments
Companies that need custom glue between tools — not another packaged platform
What We Will Not Automate Blindly
Automation without ownership and failure handling creates silent risk — we scope conservatively.
We do not rip-and-replace your entire stack in phase one unless that is the explicit project
Broken source data stays broken until naming and hygiene are addressed
Approvals that require judgment (discounts, exceptions, compliance sign-off) stay human
Tools without usable APIs may need manual steps or a different approach — we say so early
We do not invent ROI percentages; time saved depends on volume and how consistently the team uses the new path

processDescription: Automation projects fail when they try to boil the ocean. We ship the highest-ROI path first.

features.title: Discover
features.description: We inventory tools, shadow a few real workflows, and quantify where time and errors concentrate.

features.title: Design
features.description: We specify triggers, field maps, owners, and exception paths before writing integrations.

features.title: Build & integrate
features.description: We implement, test with real sample data, and train the people who will live with the workflow.

features.title: Optimize
features.description: We review failures and edge cases, then expand to adjacent processes once the foundation is stable.

faqs.question: Do we have to move to your software?
faqs.answer: No. We build automation on top of the systems you already use whenever possible. TechVerge is not selling a proprietary operations platform you must migrate into.

faqs.question: Where should we start if everything feels manual?
faqs.answer: Usually with the path that creates the most rework — often form-to-CRM, client onboarding, or status notifications. We pick one high-friction workflow, ship it well, then expand.

faqs.question: What access do you need?
faqs.answer: Read/write access to the tools in scope (or a sandbox), a process owner, and examples of correct vs incorrect records. We prefer least-privilege credentials and documented ownership.

faqs.question: Who maintains the automations after launch?
faqs.answer: We document what we built and can hand maintenance to your team, stay on for iteration, or train an internal owner. You own the accounts and the logic we implement.

faqs.question: How do you handle failures?
faqs.answer: We design alerts, retries, and human fallbacks for critical paths. Silent failure is worse than no automation — visibility is part of the build.

faqs.question: Can you work with messy spreadsheets and legacy tools?
faqs.answer: Yes, within reason. Sometimes the right first step is stabilizing data and naming conventions before full automation. We will tell you honestly if a tool needs a different approach.

title: AI SaaS & Custom Software
shortDescription: We design and build AI-powered applications and internal tools for your business — software you own, shaped around how your team actually works.
heroHeading: Custom AI-Powered Apps Built Around Your Workflows

seo.seoDescription: We design and build custom AI-powered applications and internal tools for your workflows — not a TechVerge SaaS product you subscribe to.

children.text: The Business Problem
Off-the-shelf tools stop fitting when your process is the product. Spreadsheets and patched-together apps create risk, slow delivery, and limit what AI can safely do.
Critical workflows live in fragile spreadsheets or tribal knowledge
Generic SaaS forces workarounds that your team quietly hates
You need AI features — drafting, search, classification — inside your product or ops tool
Internal tools lag behind the process, so people invent shadow systems
What We Build
We build custom software and AI-assisted features for your users or your internal teams. This is client-owned product work — not seats on a TechVerge SaaS.
Customer-facing web apps with AI-assisted workflows
Internal tools for ops, support, or sales enablement
Document and knowledge assistants grounded in your approved sources
Classification, extraction, and drafting features inside existing products
Admin panels, permissions, and audit trails suited to your org
What You Walk Away With
Client-owned software milestones you can demo — plus the architecture and handoff materials to keep building.
Scoped product brief: users, workflows, and AI feature boundaries
UX flows and data model for the agreed MVP or module
Working application increments you can review in staging
Auth, roles, and audit trails suited to the security needs we agreed
AI features with review paths where outputs need a human
Repository access, environment notes, and runbooks for ownership
How The Solution Works
We treat AI as a capability inside a product — not the product pitch. Outcomes and UX come first; models and infrastructure support them.
Clarify the job to be done
We define who the software is for, which decisions it improves, and where humans must remain in the loop.
Design product and data flows
We shape UX, permissions, and data sources so AI features stay grounded and reviewable.
Build iteratively
We ship a usable core first — auth, primary workflows, then AI features with evaluation and feedback loops.
Handoff with ownership
We document architecture, environments, and runbooks so your team (or we) can maintain and extend the system.
Example Use Cases
Internal AI ops console
A tool where staff upload documents, ask grounded questions, and trigger approved follow-up actions with an audit trail.
Customer portal with assisted workflows
Clients submit requests, get status updates, and receive AI-drafted responses that your team reviews before sending.
Domain-specific SaaS MVP
You have a clear niche workflow. We help you design and build the first production version — including AI features that differentiate the product.
Embedded AI inside an existing app
Add search, summarization, or classification to software you already run, without starting from zero.
Integrations
Custom software still has to live in your ecosystem. We plan integrations as part of the product, not as an afterthought.
Identity providers and SSO where required
CRMs, billing, and support platforms
Document stores and knowledge bases
Email, Slack, and notification channels
Analytics and logging for product and AI quality
Who It Is For
Best for teams that need software shaped to their process — including AI capabilities — and want clear ownership of what gets built.
Founders validating a niche AI-assisted product
Companies replacing fragile spreadsheets with real internal tools
Product teams embedding AI into an existing application
Operators who need custom software, not another subscription to a generic platform
Scope Boundaries We Keep Explicit
Custom software succeeds when AI is a capability inside a product — not an unbounded promise.
We do not sell seats to a TechVerge packaged SaaS — this is build work for your product or internal tool
Model outputs can be wrong; critical actions need human review unless you accept that risk in writing
Timeline expands with compliance, SSO, migrations, and poorly documented legacy systems
We will not claim user-count or revenue outcomes we have not verified
Ongoing hosting, model costs, and maintenance need an owner — us or your team — defined before launch

processDescription: Product work needs clarity on scope and ownership. We keep phases explicit so you always know what ships next.

features.title: Discover
features.description: We align on users, success metrics, constraints, and what must be custom versus integrated.

features.title: Design
features.description: We produce UX flows, data model, and AI feature boundaries — including review and escalation paths.

features.title: Build
features.description: We develop in milestones you can demo, with testing around both product behavior and AI quality.

features.title: Launch & iterate
features.description: We deploy, train users, and plan the next improvements based on real usage — not a feature dump on day one.

faqs.question: Is this TechVerge's SaaS product?
faqs.answer: No. We design and build software for you. You own the product and infrastructure decisions we agree on. We are not selling seats to a TechVerge-hosted packaged application.

faqs.question: Who owns the code and IP?
faqs.answer: Ownership is defined in the engagement agreement. In typical custom builds, you own the application we create for you, along with documentation and deployment access.

faqs.question: How do you decide what AI should and should not do?
faqs.answer: During design we mark which outputs need human review, which data sources are allowed, and which actions the system must never take automatically. Guardrails are a product decision, not an afterthought.

faqs.question: What does a realistic timeline look like?
faqs.answer: A focused MVP can often reach a usable pilot in a matter of weeks to a few months depending on integrations, compliance needs, and how defined the workflow already is. We phase delivery so you see working software early.

faqs.question: What do you need from our team?
faqs.answer: A product owner, access to subject-matter experts, sample data or documents (sanitized if needed), and clarity on users and success criteria. We can help sharpen the brief if it is still forming.

faqs.question: Can you maintain the app after launch?
faqs.answer: Yes — through an ongoing engagement — or we can hand off to your engineers with documentation and a clean repository. Maintenance expectations are set before build, not after.
